body:
m1 - CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY: the engineer's candidate 244257d is correct on the numbers that were mine. I re-derived on a clean detached worktree at their exact SHA, computed the quantities myself rather than reading their assertions, then destroyed the worktree.

  chronology   value 0.039516  support 0.304620  cond 0.913861  total 3.000000
  specificity  massWeighted 0.678220  meanOfRatios 0.628359  cond 2.736038

All six match what they posted. The discriminator I was most worried about is LIVE: per-unit source masses are 0.7424 / 0.0832 / 0.9955 / 0.9150 - four distinct values out of four - and the formula gap is 0.0499. Stemming did not equalise source mass, so the assertion the compression and specificity rulings rest on still discriminates rather than passing vacuously.

So my published chronology finding settles at 0.0395 on 30.5% support, not 0.0468 on 25.6%. Less dramatic than I reported it, still the point.

ONE REVIEW FINDING I SENT THEM, not blocking: AnnaFixtureSuite's guard computes its expectation with the same expression the implementation uses, so it pins the wiring but cannot fail for any change to Lexical.stems. An identity stemmer would pass it and put the fixture straight back to raw lemmas - the exact defect being fixed. I suggested one non-self-referential line naming a concrete stem.

AND A NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING, because it is the fourth time tonight this exact move has paid. My first instinct was to recommend asserting every lemma equals its own stem - the check I used to FIND the original bug. I ran it against their tree before recommending it: 2 of 21 fail, `hous` and `nois`. THE STEMMER IS NOT IDEMPOTENT - stem("house") = "hous", stem("hous") = "hou". My proposed assertion would have failed on correct output and sent them chasing a non-bug.

The pattern across all four: the thing I am about to recommend to someone else is exactly what I should run first. Reading a branch tells you what the code allows; running it tells you what it does - your formulation, and it applies to advice as much as to findings. I have now been wrong in both directions with it tonight: inferred occurrence from permission on the placement threshold, and would have inferred breakage from a proxy here.

I did flag one real hazard to them off the back of it: nodeLemmasFrom must never be applied to an already-derived lemma set, because double-stemming silently shortens every lemma with no error.

Nothing outstanding from me. ac71674 is still pending your gate; my other four beads await your rulings and none of them is blocking me.
